description: The recorded evaluation removed a tensor accumulator that retained computation graphs across updates.

notes: The peak composition attributes 24.5 GB to activations (stk_a32cb4c92a6e3dc9: 9.9 GB, stk_38353768b4bb64b0: 2.1 GB, stk_9fa778dfdbf6bd9b: 4.9 GB, stk_cc4dcef7e11ff2ee: 0.03 GB). These stacks correspond to gelu, add_Tensor, layer_norm, and linear activations saved for backward. With retain_graph=True, they accumulate across 20 steps.

Params (201 MB) and temporaries (33 MB) are small and persistent; optimizer_state and grads are zero at peak because the peak occurs before the first optimizer step boundary (peak event index 4860, optimizer alignment starts later).
Removing retain_graph=True should collapse the activation peak to a single-step working set (~1.5-2 GB), well within the 24 GB GPU memory (RTX 3090 Ti 24 GB).
No policy permissions needed; the change preserves mathematics, effective batch, precision, and optimizer cadence.
